misconceptions.description: Assuming an AI answer is correct because it is stated fluently and confidently
misconceptions.trigger: teacher accepts an AI-generated fact, citation, or standard alignment without verifying it
misconceptions.feedback: Generative models state wrong answers with the same confidence as right ones and can fabricate citations. Verify any factual or standards claim against an authoritative source before using it with students.

misconceptions.description: Equating AI literacy with knowing how to operate a specific app or write prompts
misconceptions.trigger: teacher claims AI literacy after learning the buttons of one product
misconceptions.feedback: AI literacy is the judgment to decide when a tool fits, what it cannot do, and how it affects students. Operating an app is necessary but not sufficient.

misconceptions.description: Believing a model understands meaning rather than predicting likely text from patterns
misconceptions.trigger: teacher attributes reasoning or intent to a model's output
misconceptions.feedback: Generative AI predicts plausible continuations; it does not understand content or check truth. Frame its output as a draft to evaluate, not knowledge to trust.

misconceptions.description: Treating teacher AI literacy as private rather than something to model openly for students
misconceptions.trigger: teacher uses AI but hides the verification and judgment steps from students
misconceptions.feedback: Make your verification visible. Modeling how you check, accept, and reject AI output teaches students the critical-use habits that are the point of AI literacy.
